MISSION: Help maintenance engineers understand, apply, and realize the 6 reliability-centred maintenance strategies, and answer their real questions about them.

PRINCIPLES.en: Base intervention on measured asset condition rather than elapsed time.
PRINCIPLES.apply: Instrument the asset, set an alarm threshold from real failure data, and intervene when the threshold is crossed.

PRINCIPLES.short: Find the P-F interval before you plan
PRINCIPLES.en: Know how long an asset runs between detectable potential failure and functional failure.
PRINCIPLES.apply: Derive the interval from real failure history, then set inspection frequency below it.

PRINCIPLES.short: Schedule only where failure is age-related
PRINCIPLES.en: Time-based replacement helps only when failure probability genuinely rises with age.
PRINCIPLES.apply: Plot the hazard curve from real data; if it is flat, scheduled replacement adds cost and risk without benefit.

PRINCIPLES.short: Every task must change an outcome
PRINCIPLES.en: A maintenance task that cannot change the failure outcome is waste however diligently performed.
PRINCIPLES.apply: For each task ask what failure it prevents or detects; delete it if the answer is neither.

PRINCIPLES.short: Run-to-failure is a decision, not neglect
PRINCIPLES.en: For low-consequence assets, deliberate run-to-failure is the correct strategy.
PRINCIPLES.apply: Record the consequence assessment that justified it, so the choice is auditable rather than assumed.

PRINCIPLES.en: Safety and environmental consequences change the acceptable failure probability, not just the cost case.
PRINCIPLES.apply: Classify each failure mode by consequence before selecting any task.

rcm.note: The evaluation criteria an RCM process must satisfy.

weibull.name: Weibull hazard analysis
weibull.note: Used to test whether failure is genuinely age-related.

iso14224.name: ISO 14224 failure data collection
iso14224.note: Standardised taxonomy for equipment failure records.

RELATIONS.evidence: Condition monitoring is only actionable once the P-F interval sets the inspection frequency.
The hazard curve test for age-related failure is a Weibull shape-parameter question.
Run-to-failure is only admissible after consequence classification clears it.
The outcome test is what removes scheduled tasks that the hazard curve does not justify.
